immutability_policy: Thresholds, expected labels, splits, and adopted source checksums are never edited in place. A scientific change requires a new collection version.

threshold_revisions.scope: membrane_orientation gates only; no record, source, split or expectation changed
change: normal_drift_across_20_rotations_deg_max renamed to normal_drift_across_5_rotations_deg_max (value unchanged at 1.0)
threshold_revisions.evidence: The achieved accuracy is bimodal with an empty band four orders of magnitude wide. Across 16 beta_barrel cases the mean unsigned normal error is <= 0.057 deg on x86_64 and <= 0.038 deg on arm64 for every case that converges, and >= 5.618 deg for every case that does not. Nothing falls between 0.06 and 5.6 deg on either architecture. The method does not degrade gracefully: it either recovers the normal essentially exactly or misses by degrees. The superseded 15.0 deg threshold sat inside the failure mode and could not separate the two populations -- 1QD6 passed every gate on arm64 with an 8.391 deg error while x86_64 recorded 0.000115 deg for the same case.
threshold_revisions.rationale: 1.0 deg is above the converged population by more than an order of magnitude and below the failure population by a factor of five, so it separates them without sitting on either. It is also defensible against the reference rather than only against this dataset: OPM's own orientational uncertainty for well-ordered barrels is of this order, and at a typical barrel radius of ~12 A a 1 deg tilt displaces rim residue depth by 12*sin(1 deg) = 0.21 A -- well under one residue layer and small against the ~5 A interface width the zone assignment depends on. The per-case bound is held at twice the mean bound, preserving the original intent that a single case may deviate further than the panel average; 2.0 deg is 0.42 A of rim displacement, still sub-residue.
threshold_revisions.rename_rationale: The drift gate was named for 20 rotations while memorient's five_fold_validate performs 5, and every adopted case records exactly 5. The name asserted a protocol the evidence does not perform. The value is unchanged; only the name is corrected to match what is measured. Raising the rotation count to 20 would be a stronger test of rotational stability and is recorded as a future scientific improvement, not made here, because it would change what the gate measures rather than what it is called.
threshold_revisions.note: Recorded rather than edited silently, per immutability_policy. No adopted record, source checksum, split or expectation is altered; only the pass criteria for the membrane_orientation workflow move, and the superseded values are kept above.

membrane_orientation.reference: OPM, which distributes structures already oriented on Z and records its fitted half-thickness as a REMARK in the file.
membrane_orientation.note: The panel now asks two independent questions and both are gated at 1.0 degree: accuracy against OPM (mean_unsigned_normal_error_deg_max) and reproducibility under rotation (normal_drift_across_5_rotations_deg_max). They are different quantities and a case can fail either alone -- 1BXW is 6.19 degrees from OPM on x86_64 while drifting only 0.015 degrees under rotation, and 2F1C sits 5.6 degrees from OPM on arm64 while drifting 5.09. The accuracy bound was 15.0 degrees in collection 2.0, which sat inside the failure mode and passed 1QD6 on arm64 at 8.391 degrees; see threshold_revisions. Note that memorient's own validation.normal_threshold_deg has always been 1.0 degree on the error, so the panel now holds the workflow to the standard the module itself declares rather than to one fifteen times looser.
membrane_orientation.vacuity_note: A Jaccard over an empty reference set is 1.0 and means nothing, so a minimum extracellular reference size is required before the floor applies. 1THQ was excluded for carrying only 7 reference residues.

missing_evidence_behavior.rule: The run's missing-evidence list must equal the stratum's declared expectation.
missing_evidence_behavior.note: memorient reports external_opm_ppm_benchmark_adoption missing on every run: it is a constant in the CLI, not a state check. It is therefore declared expected. The consequence worth recording is that the module cannot signal the opposite -- this panel IS the OPM adoption, and memorient will keep reporting the benchmark unadopted after it is adopted, because nothing connects the two. Making that flag conditional on an adopted source record is an open defect, not something this panel can fix by curation.

coverage_requirements.rationale: non_trivial_normal_error is the load-bearing one: fifteen of the sixteen structures recover OPM's normal to about 0.0001 degrees, so a panel without 1BXW would test the gate against nothing but exact agreement and could not distinguish a working fit from one that returns the input orientation unchanged.

panels.stratum_scope_note: Only the beta_barrel stratum is adopted. alpha_helical is explicitly non-blocking for Mark 1 and its qualification v1 result failed the normal-error gate at 31.6 degrees against a 15 degree limit, so it is curated separately rather than adopted alongside a stratum that passes.

alternatives.matches_declared_expectation: The computed identity must equal the value declared for the case. A declared engineered mutation is expected to lower identity, and failing to lower it is the defect.
alternatives.equals_one: Identity must be 1.0 for every case. Disqualifies every structure carrying an engineered mutation, including 2V7A, and with it the panel's only nonstandard-residue coverage.

residue_identity.chosen_because: 2V7A measures 0.996296, which is exactly 1 - 1/270: the single declared T315I difference and nothing else. Detecting a declared mutation is the behaviour under test, so the gate asserts the measurement matches what the case declares.

alphafold.note: No wwPDB validation report exists for a predicted model. The official confidence evidence is pLDDT in the B-factor column plus the PAE matrix, so the gate checks those instead of geometry-validation metrics.

cryo_em.note: A cryo-EM validation report carries the same geometry metrics as an x-ray one plus a reported resolution, but no crystallographic R-factors. Resolution is required here because the report supplies it; requiring r_free would fail every case in the stratum.

nmr.note: A solution-NMR validation report carries geometry metrics but neither resolution nor R-factors, because neither exists for the method. The metric set is the geometry core alone.

missing_evidence_behavior.rule: The run's missing-evidence list must equal the stratum's declared expectation. Evidence that cannot exist for a stratum is declared, not silently tolerated; anything else appearing there is a change that must be noticed.
missing_evidence_behavior.detail: Exit 1 is a scientifically-incomplete result carrying its reason, not a failure.

nmr.rationale: An NMR entry deposits an ensemble; these range from 10 to 20 models. StructQC evaluates one model, so which one is a scientific choice and is declared per case rather than inherited from a CLI default. Model index 0 (the first deposited model) is used uniformly. Ensemble-wide agreement is a separate question this stratum does not test.

coverage_requirements.rationale: The panel's coverage_rules were prose only. Composition counts records per stratum and split, so a coverage rule could go unmet while the panel reported itself complete -- and insertion codes did exactly that until 1IGT was curated. Each feature is now witnessed from the evidence an executed case produced, and execution fails if any required feature has no witness.

modified_residues.status: NOT SATISFIED - recorded as an open defect, not as met coverage
modified_residues.why_not_witnessed: StructQC counts a residue as nonstandard only when its one-letter code is X. A chemically modified residue that maps to its unmodified parent is normalised and never reported. 2V7A chain A contains PTR393 (phosphotyrosine); gemmi sees 271 polymer residues, StructQC reports 270 with nonstandard_residues: 0, and the string PTR appears nowhere in the evidence record, the residue table, or the run manifest.
modified_residues.why_not_worked_around: A detector could read the coordinate file directly, but then the panel would claim coverage of a feature the tool under test does not report. Coverage must be witnessed from the evidence the tool produces, or it is not coverage.
modified_residues.resolution: Either StructQC reports modified residues explicitly, or the panel's coverage_rules drop the claim. For a coordinate-trust tool, a post-translational modification is exactly what a user needs surfaced before mapping a functional residue, so reporting it is the better fix.

coverage_rules: Every catalytic residue and role is frozen from a cited M-CSA release before execution.
Apo, modified, and incomplete controls must preserve missing or unresolved evidence.

functional_site.note: The recovery floor is written for complete structures. The apo/modified/incomplete stratum exists to carry structures whose curated residues cannot all be resolved -- 1ALG resolves none of five -- so applying the floor there would fail the stratum for doing its job. Those cases are held to their declared per-site states instead, which is the stricter test.
functional_site.cofactor_declaration_source: UniProt COFACTOR annotation, joined to PDB component ids through an explicit ChEBI table. Declaring from UniProt rather than from the coordinate file is what makes the gate non-vacuous: a cofactor the structure lacks is still declared and reported not_observed.
functional_site.component_map_note: Every case supplies the ChEBI-to-component map, not only the metal stratum. Without it a declared cofactor resolves to "unresolved" rather than "not_observed", which would let an apo or fragment structure look merely unmapped instead of missing its cofactor.

missing_evidence_behavior.rule: No pocket predictor is run, so every case reports pocket_results missing. Declared per stratum so the absence is stated, not tolerated.

coverage_requirements.rationale: The panel's coverage_rules were prose, and composition counts records per stratum and split, so a rule could go unmet while the panel reported itself complete. That is exactly how insertion codes hid in the StructQC panel. Each feature is witnessed from the evidence an executed case produced, and execution fails if any required feature has no witness.

curated_residue_missing_coordinates.declared_by: the panel's coverage_rules, as incomplete controls
curated_residue_missing_coordinates.status: NOT SATISFIED - recorded rather than claimed
curated_residue_missing_coordinates.why_not_witnessed: 1ALG's curated residues fall outside the modelled fragment entirely, so site-context reports unresolved_mapping. missing_coordinates needs a residue inside the reference map but disordered in the coordinates.
curated_residue_missing_coordinates.resolution: Curate a structure with a disordered catalytic residue.

curated_residue_substituted.was: recorded unwitnessable while the panel held only twelve cases
curated_residue_substituted.now: witnessed by 4JDW, a C407A substitution of glycine amidinotransferase. It was recorded as unsatisfiable because every substituted structure found duplicated a homolog group already in the panel; 4JDW does not, because P50440 entered the panel through the apo/modified stratum rather than a mechanism stratum.

panels.annotation_policy: M-CSA annotations and their ChEBI-to-component maps are committed, not acquired. The panel's coverage_rules require every catalytic residue and role to be frozen from a cited M-CSA release before execution, and re-fetching them at execution time would let an upstream curation change silently move an expectation. They are generated by tools/harvest_mcsa_annotations.py, carry the entry and URL they came from, and are digest-locked like any other artifact.

coverage_rules: Operator expansion and stoichiometry are compared with deposited mmCIF metadata.
SASA is compared with a checksum-pinned standalone FreeSASA calculation.

expected_result.exit_code_reason: complete: every declared evidence leg was supplied

assembly_interface.note: The SASA gate is checked against the FreeSASA command line, not against the module's own earlier output. assembly-context records only that FreeSASA was 'available_invoked' with no version, so the executor captures the version and treats it as part of the expectation: a tolerance against a reference implementation is meaningless without knowing which build produced the reference.

stratum_definition.homodimer: exactly two polymer chains with one distinct sequence
stratum_definition.heterooligomer: two or three polymer chains with more than one distinct sequence
stratum_definition.tetramer: exactly four polymer chains, whether homo- or heteromeric
stratum_definition.note: The four strata overlap unless the boundary is stated: 1QUM is four chains of four distinct entities and satisfies both 'tetramer' and 'heterooligomer' by their plain reading. Chain count is taken as decisive above two, so a four-chain complex is a tetramer regardless of composition, and heterooligomer covers the small mixed complexes that chain count alone would not distinguish.

freesasa_processability.policy: Cases are selected from structures FreeSASA can process, and which those are is determined by running it.

excluded.5ICD: FreeSASA aborts with an internal assertion on atomic radii.

freesasa_processability.note: The failure is not simply 'contains ligands': 1QPR carries MN, PHT and PPC and processes cleanly, while 5ICD (ICT, MG) and 1NZY (BCA, CA, EDO, PO4) abort. assembly-context exits 2 and reports the failure rather than emitting a surface number, which is the correct behaviour and is why the panel can exclude these rather than silently mis-measure them.

missing_evidence_behavior.rule: Declared per stratum so a legitimately absent leg is stated, not tolerated.

coverage_requirements.rationale: Pilot coverage; extended when the remaining strata are curated.

coverage_rules: Exactly four unrelated protein families are represented, with one independently curated judgment in each relationship stratum per family.
Foldseek and DIAMOND execute as separate checksum-bound evidence legs.

candidate_migrations.reason: Qualification v1 artifacts remain useful curation candidates but do not satisfy v2 split, mapping, stratum, or expected-result metadata by themselves.
